inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,840 Python-split logical lines of the normalized paper. The source supports 28 semantic units: two immutable v1 carries and 26 fresh units spanning the local-statistics bridge, exact characteristic-polynomial generating functions, cumulant and Gaussian-limit mechanisms, finite-size corrections, arithmetic-factor separation, numerical calibration, magnitude-tail regimes, and COE/CSE symmetry-class extensions. Formula extraction is imperfect but most mechanisms are recoverable from checked prose; exact symbolic reuse of flagged spans requires scan verification.

sections_inspected.label: front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic matter plus an abstract-level map of exact CUE moments, Gaussian limits, zeta comparison, and ensemble extensions.

sections_inspected.label: 1 Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Motivates the local zero-statistics transfer, states Selberg and moment targets, summarizes exact CUE results, separates local random-matrix and long-range prime effects, and marks symmetry-family limits.

sections_inspected.label: 2.1 Generating functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives exact modulus and phase generating functions from Haar eigenphase densities through Selberg-type integral transformations.

sections_inspected.label: 2.2 Value distribution of Re log Z
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transforms the modulus generating function into moments, cumulants, density, large-N Gaussianity, and asymmetric finite-N corrections.

sections_inspected.label: 2.3 Value distribution of Im log Z
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives parity-constrained cumulants, the eigenvalue-counting bridge, Gaussianity, exact symmetry, and a faster correction scale.

sections_inspected.label: 2.4 Independence
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses a joint generating function and mixed-cumulant scaling to prove asymptotic independence of real and imaginary parts.

sections_inspected.label: 2.5 Asymptotics of the generating functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Packages leading modulus and phase moment coefficients with Barnes G-functions, including analytic continuation and pole/zero structure.

sections_inspected.label: 3 zeta(1/2+it)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Calibrates matrix size by mean spacing, compares finite-N predictions with zeta data, restores prime factors, and distinguishes bulk, near-zero, and tail regimes.

sections_inspected.label: 4 COE and CSE Results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Extends generating functions, cumulants, Gaussian limits, variances, and leading moment coefficients across circular symmetry classes.

sections_inspected.label: acknowledgements and references
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Non-unit-bearing acknowledgements, page furniture, and bibliography.

accepted_units.title: Local zero statistics motivate characteristic-polynomial value transfer
accepted_units.why_material: Connects mean-spacing-scaled zeta zeros to CUE eigenphases and makes the reusable but explicitly local inference from spectral correlations to characteristic-polynomial value statistics.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span. The sentence announcing the comparison targets continues through line 90, and Selberg's target is stated at lines 98-111; record the bounded repair rather than changing this span.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The scaled-eigenphase notation is split across lines 83-86 by a control character, but the surrounding prose recovers the local-statistics claim; verify the exact displayed scaling against the scan before symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: Selberg Gaussian limit does not erase systematic finite-height deviations
accepted_units.why_material: Pairs the independent Gaussian limiting law with the observed growth of finite-height moment deviations, establishing why a finite-size surrogate is a substantive target rather than a cosmetic approximation.
accepted_units.context_note: Read as the explicit theorem target announced by the preceding introduction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (3) is formula-degraded, but lines 105-111 state the independent zero-mean unit-variance Gaussian limit and the finite-height deviation in recoverable prose.

accepted_units.title: Zeta moments are normalized into an arithmetic factor and an unknown coefficient
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the moment-coefficient problem in a form that later permits a clean separation between arithmetic Euler-product data and a universal random-matrix coefficient.
accepted_units.context_note: Known and conjectured integer values supply the comparison points later matched by the CUE coefficient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed product and powers are OCR-sensitive; prose and the listed special values are usable, but exact transcription of equations (4)-(5) needs scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Two exact CUE generators encode modulus and argument statistics
accepted_units.why_material: States the finite-N gamma-product generators for absolute value and phase, and makes the logarithm branch convention and eigenphase jump explicit; these are the analytic engines for all later distributions.
accepted_units.context_note: The modulus generator is a Mellin-type moment object while the phase ratio generator encodes Im log Z.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Gamma-product typography is degraded; the branch prescription in lines 149-152 is prose-stable, while exact products should be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Mean-density matching fixes matrix size and separates universal from arithmetic effects
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies N with log(T/2π), interprets finite-height zeta behavior through finite-degree CUE polynomials, and isolates random-matrix short-range effects from prime-driven long-range corrections in the moment conjecture.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span. Its opening depends on the Gaussian result at lines 153-155, and its final numerical-support sentence completes at line 241; record the repair without changing the carried span.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several displayed formulas are OCR-degraded, but the density match and two-factor mechanism are explicitly recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: Low-lying family statistics require the compact group selected by symmetry
accepted_units.why_material: Limits naive CUE transfer by explaining that averaging low zeros across L-function families may select orthogonal or symplectic groups, so the correct characteristic-polynomial model depends on family symmetry.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a proposed extension to other L-function families, not evidence that the CUE description applies universally.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: No material formula dependency; group names and the averaging regime are prose-stable.

accepted_units.title: Haar eigenphase integration becomes a Selberg integral for |Z| moments
accepted_units.why_material: Shows the reusable derivation chain from a characteristic-polynomial eigenvalue product, through the CUE joint density and trigonometric coordinates, to a Selberg integral and exact gamma product.
accepted_units.context_note: The material value is the representation change and parameter matching, not the routine intervening algebra alone.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (21)-(26) contain damaged symbols and spacing; the coordinate changes and final analytic-continuation conclusion are prose-recoverable, but exact constants and exponents need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A branch-controlled sine series converts the phase generator to Selberg form
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the argument generator by fixing the logarithm branch, evaluating its sine series, and transforming the Haar integral into the second exact gamma product.
accepted_units.context_note: The branch range is essential: without it the phase random variable and its jumps are ambiguous.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Control characters split the transformed-angle notation across lines 404-432, and equations (27)-(33) are formula-risky; retain the checked prose mechanism and require scan verification for exact symbolic reuse.

accepted_units.title: One generator yields moments, cumulants, and the full density through three transforms
accepted_units.why_material: Makes explicit the reusable interface from Taylor coefficients of M_N to moments, derivatives of log M_N to cumulants, and Fourier inversion to the value density.
accepted_units.context_note: The polygamma representation begins the asymptotic analysis used in the next units.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The transform formulas are legible in structure but symbol-level transcription should be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Variance grows logarithmically while higher real-part cumulants stabilize
accepted_units.why_material: Separates the divergent second cumulant from bounded higher cumulants using integral representations and rescaling, which is the key scale separation behind Gaussian normalization.
accepted_units.context_note: The source also explains how arbitrarily many inverse-N terms can be generated, though only representative terms are displayed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact coefficients in equations (42)-(48) are formula-sensitive; the logarithmic-versus-bounded asymptotic distinction is prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Normalized higher cumulants vanish and leave a Gaussian Fourier kernel
accepted_units.why_material: Provides the conceptual proof of the real-part central limit: after variance normalization every cumulant above order two disappears, so Fourier inversion converges to the Gaussian density.
accepted_units.context_note: This isolates the proof mechanism from the subsequent finite-N correction analysis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Fourier formulas are OCR-affected, but the normalized-cumulant argument and conclusion are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Odd cumulants create asymmetric finite-N corrections before the Gaussian limit
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how retaining higher cumulants produces a correction expansion, identifies the leading (log N)^(-3/2) deviation, and traces finite-N asymmetry to odd powers, including an Airy resummation of the cubic term.
accepted_units.context_note: The Airy form is an alternative leading approximation rather than a new limiting law.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The detailed coefficient and Airy formulas are extraction-risky; the correction order, odd-cumulant cause, and asymmetry are prose-stable.

accepted_units.title: Exponentiating the cumulant series recovers the Gaussian moment hierarchy
accepted_units.why_material: Closes the analytic loop by showing how cumulants reconstruct moments and why even moments have the Gaussian leading relation while odd moments are lower order.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a compact reusable bridge between two statistical representations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (56) is formula-sensitive, but the exponential-series procedure is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Argument cumulants have exact parity and equal eigenvalue-count fluctuations
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the vanishing of all odd cumulants for Im log Z, relates even cumulants to the real-part calculation, and identifies Im log Z differences with fluctuations of eigenvalue counts in arcs.
accepted_units.context_note: The counting-function identity explains why an earlier random-matrix Gaussian theorem applies to the argument observable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact counting identity and constants are formula-sensitive; parity, Gaussianity, and the observable bridge are prose-recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Exact evenness removes cubic corrections and accelerates Gaussian convergence
accepted_units.why_material: Connects the identically zero odd cumulants to an even finite-N density and a (log N)^(-2) correction scale, asymptotically smaller than for the real part.
accepted_units.context_note: The comparison with the real part turns a symmetry statement into a quantitative convergence prediction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Expansion coefficients are formula-risky, while the evenness and relative correction order are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Mixed cumulants vanish after scaling, yielding independent Gaussian components
accepted_units.why_material: Constructs the joint modulus-phase generator, evaluates it in Selberg form, and shows that normalized mixed terms vanish so the bivariate density factors into two Gaussian densities.
accepted_units.context_note: This proves asymptotic independence rather than inferring it from the two marginal Gaussian limits.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several joint-density symbols are split by control characters at lines 872-923; the mixed-cumulant scaling and factorized conclusion at lines 929-940 are recoverable, but exact formulas need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Barnes G compresses the universal leading coefficient of modulus moments
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies the N-normalized CUE modulus moment coefficient with a Barnes G ratio, extends it analytically, exposes its pole structure, and reduces integer values to factorial products matching known zeta coefficients.
accepted_units.context_note: The matching values motivate, but do not independently prove, the zeta moment conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Gamma and Barnes G typography is degraded; prose identifies the continuation, poles, and integer-product reduction, while exact formulas require scan checking.

accepted_units.title: The phase generator has a symmetric Barnes G leading coefficient and zero lattice
accepted_units.why_material: Carries the same compression method to the argument generator, where parity produces a symmetric Barnes G product and a structured set of zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: This supplies the random-matrix factor later paired with an arithmetic product for phase moments.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exponent placement and zero statement are formula-sensitive; verify equations (89)-(91) before exact use.

accepted_units.title: Density-matched finite N explains deviations that the limiting Gaussian misses
accepted_units.why_material: Uses the mean-spacing map to select N≈42 and reports that exact finite-N CUE densities and moments track high-zero zeta data better than the asymptotic Gaussian, including the real/imaginary asymmetry contrast.
accepted_units.context_note: Figures and tables at lines 1126-1238 are supporting evidence; the inference remains an empirical finite-height calibration.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose comparison is stable; exact plotted or tabulated values depend on the extracted figures and tables.

accepted_units.title: Long-range prime effects multiply the finite-N universal moment factor
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why local random-matrix information is incomplete, derives the need for an independent prime product under a truncated Euler-product heuristic, and combines it with the Barnes G CUE coefficient.
accepted_units.context_note: The independence of prime contributions is a stated heuristic, and famous-theorem agreement is calibration rather than novel validation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact Euler and Barnes products are formula-risky; the multiplicative decomposition and evidence status are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Adding the arithmetic factor improves real-part moment predictions
accepted_units.why_material: Defines real-part moments by differentiating the product of the CUE and arithmetic generators and compares CUE-only versus CUE-plus-primes predictions against the same numerical data.
accepted_units.context_note: The table is a finite-height comparison and does not establish the asymptotic conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Table 4 is legible enough for the qualitative comparison, while exact equation transcription remains formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: A separate arithmetic product corrects phase moments and matches low-order checks
accepted_units.why_material: Constructs the phase analogue of the multiplicative model, reports improved finite-height moments, and checks consistency with the second-moment formula and independent low-order heuristics.
accepted_units.context_note: The final displayed limit is a conjecture assembled from the CUE phase factor and the arithmetic product.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The product b(λ) and limiting formula are OCR-sensitive; the improvement and low-order consistency checks are prose-stable.

accepted_units.title: Saddle and pole regimes separate bulk lognormal behavior from near-zero mass
accepted_units.why_material: Fourier inversion gives a large-N lognormal-type bulk approximation, while the nearest pole controls the fixed-N near-zero limit; the source explicitly diagnoses why exchanging the N and w limits invalidates the bulk approximation.
accepted_units.context_note: The figure is supporting calibration; the reusable mechanism is the saddle-versus-pole and nonuniform-limit distinction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact constants and pole residues are formula-sensitive, but the two asymptotic regimes and failure condition are prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: The arithmetic product affects near-zero and tail probabilities more than the bulk
accepted_units.why_material: Multiplies the magnitude transform by the arithmetic factor, checks the near-zero correction numerically, and uses the saddle location to explain why the prime contribution is pushed toward the tail for large N.
accepted_units.context_note: This refines the universal-times-arithmetic split at the distributional rather than moment level.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Numerical constants and transform notation should be scan-checked; the tail-localization argument is prose-stable.

accepted_units.title: A single circular-ensemble parameter preserves the Gaussian mechanism across CUE, COE, and CSE
accepted_units.why_material: Generalizes the exact generators and cumulants to three circular ensembles, showing that logarithmic variance with bounded higher cumulants yields Gaussian real and imaginary parts in every symmetry class.
accepted_units.context_note: The calculation transfers the mechanism while changing symmetry-dependent coefficients.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The ensemble parameter glyph is missing in many formulas, but prose anchors its values to CUE, COE, and CSE; exact beta-dependent products need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: COE and CSE change the variance scale and constant term
accepted_units.why_material: Computes the next variance asymptotics separately for symplectic and orthogonal ensembles, including the even/odd matrix-size issue, while retaining equality of real and imaginary variances.
accepted_units.context_note: This identifies exactly where symmetry affects finite-size calibration despite a shared Gaussian limit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Polygamma coefficients and constants are formula-dependent and require scan verification; the need for separate symmetry-class calculations is clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: CSE leading moment coefficients have distinct gamma/Barnes G and zero structures
accepted_units.why_material: Derives symplectic leading coefficients for modulus and phase generators, identifies the moment subsequence yielding rational values, and checks pole and zero multiplicities against the finite-N products.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a formula-level refinement of the symmetry-class generalization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The source is heavily formula-dependent here and the ensemble parameter is partly lost; use the prose pole/zero and rationality statements, and scan-verify every exact special-function formula.

accepted_units.title: COE leading coefficients shift the moment subsequence and pole/zero pattern
accepted_units.why_material: Provides the orthogonal analogue, with different normalization, rational moment subsequence, and analytic pole/zero structure for modulus and phase generators.
accepted_units.context_note: Together with the CSE unit, this shows that Gaussian universality does not imply identical moment constants.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact gamma/Barnes G formulas and multiplicities are formula-sensitive; all should be verified against the scan before symbolic use.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Density-matched finite-size universality plus arithmetic correction
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Mean-spacing matching selects a finite CUE surrogate for local universal behavior, while a separate Euler-product factor restores long-range arithmetic effects in zeta moments.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The prime independence step is heuristic, agreement at famous moment values is calibration, and finite-height numerical fit does not prove the asymptotic factorization.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Cumulant parity predicts both shape and convergence speed
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Bounded higher cumulants yield Gaussian normalization, but exact disappearance of odd phase cumulants enforces finite-N evenness and removes the slower cubic correction; mixed-cumulant decay separately gives independence.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: These rates and independence are established for the CUE characteristic-polynomial model, not automatically for finite-height zeta values.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Symmetry class changes constants without changing the Gaussian mechanism
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Orthogonal, unitary, and symplectic models share logarithmic variance plus bounded higher cumulants, yet differ in variance constants, admissible rational moment subsequences, and pole/zero patterns.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Applying a non-CUE class to an L-function requires an independently justified family-symmetry assignment, and exact special-function formulas are extraction-sensitive.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Transform singularities distinguish bulk, near-zero, and arithmetic-tail behavior
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Fourier/Mellin inversion links analytic generator structure to distributional regimes: a saddle controls the bulk, the nearest pole controls fixed-N near-zero values, and the arithmetic multiplier is most visible away from the large-N bulk.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The approximations are nonuniform in N and magnitude, so exchanging limits or extending the saddle formula to the origin is invalid.
